Not all women with synchronous primary cancers of the endometrium and ovary have Lynch syndrome, but they are at increased risk. Lynch syndrome, also known as hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer (HNPCC), is a genetic disorder that increases the risk of developing certain types of cancer, including endometrial and ovarian cancer. 

Studies have shown that approximately 10-15% of women with synchronous endometrial and ovarian cancers may have Lynch syndrome. However, many cases of synchronous endometrial and ovarian cancers are not associated with Lynch syndrome and may be attributed to other genetic or environmental factors.

Therefore, women with synchronous primary cancers of the endometrium and ovary should be considered for genetic counseling and testing for Lynch syndrome, but a diagnosis of Lynch syndrome cannot be assumed solely based on the presence of these cancers.
